# API Compatibility Regression

How projects measure API surface breakage across versions.

## Kubernetes API Stability Guarantees

The deprecation policy defines explicit timelines by stability level [49]:

| Level | Minimum Lifetime | Deprecation Window | Removal Window |
|---|---|---|---|
| GA (stable) | Indefinite within major version | No time limit after deprecation | Only on major version change |
| Beta | ~18 months total | ≤9 months or 3 releases after introduction | ≤9 months or 3 releases after deprecation |
| Alpha | None | May be removed any release | May be removed any release |

Since Kubernetes has never incremented past major version v1, GA APIs are effectively permanent [49].

Historical API removal timeline shows typical 2-3 years between deprecation and removal across v1.22-v1.32 [54].

## Monitoring: Deprecated API Usage

Prometheus metric `apiserver_requested_deprecated_apis` [49] [50]:
- Type: Gauge
- Stability: STABLE
- Labels: `group`, `version`, `resource`, `subresource`, `removed_release`
- Available since: v1.19

Additional signals:
- Warning header in API responses (RFC 7234) since v1.19 [49]
- Audit annotation: `k8s.io/deprecated: true` [49]
- Deprecated metrics hidden at N+3 release, accessible via `--show-hidden-metrics-for-version` flag [75]

**Caveat:** The garbage collector creates noise via reflection-based API reads — filter when analyzing user usage [49].

| Feb 2018 | 53 | 481 | 11% |

Source: [15]

This measures whether each API endpoint has at least one conformance test, not functional depth per endpoint.

## Static Analysis Tools

Three tools detect deprecated/removed API usage before upgrades:

| Tool | Detection Method | CI Integration | Limitations |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Pluto** [51] | Scans IaC repos and Helm releases via `versions.yaml` database | GitHub Actions (`pluto detect-files`) | Cannot query API server (auto-converts versions); limited CRD support (only cert-manager, some Istio) |
| **Kubent** [52] | Reads `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` annotations and Helm secrets/configmaps via Rego policies | `--exit-error` flag | Requires explicit file names, cannot scan directories; no local Helm chart support |
| **Kubepug** [53] | Downloads `data.json` (64KB) refreshed every 30 minutes from K8s API definitions | kubectl krew plugin (`kubectl deprecations`) | Detects via code comments (+k8s:prerelease-lifecycle-gen), supports air-gapped environments |

All three share a fundamental limitation: static analysis cannot detect runtime behavioral changes or dynamic API usage.

## OpenShift API Compatibility

OpenShift Compatibility Level 1: Stable within major release for minimum 12 months or 3 minor releases (whichever longer). Objects stored in etcd using removed APIs become read-only — they cannot be modified or updated until migrated [55].

## Counter-Perspectives

**Conformance tests have limited coverage:**
- Only ~5-6% of total e2e test suite [12] [16]
- Implementation-specific features explicitly excluded from conformance [discovery agent, Tier 1]

**Behavioral regressions bypass specification conformance:**
- Contract tests catch structural drift but miss semantic/behavioral changes
- Auth regressions are "silent failures" unless explicitly tested
- API field behavior can change without version change (e.g., field topology transitions) [discovery agent, Tier 1]

**Real-world upgrade failures despite proper deprecation:**
- Helm fails when client library cannot parse deprecated objects [discovery agent, Tier 1]
- Azure AKS issue #3984: cluster upgrade blocked by deprecated API, `forceUpgrade` bypass causes API calls to fail [discovery agent, Tier 2]
- Deprecated API removal still causes breaking changes even with 2-3 year warning [55]

**Static analysis misses runtime constraints:**
- Academic research shows static analysis misses runtime-specific constraints; dynamic approach needed for precision [discovery agent, Tier 1]

## Metric Taxonomy

| Metric | Type | Measurable By |
|---|---|---|
| `apiserver_requested_deprecated_apis` | Continuous gauge | Operator (Prometheus) |
| API deprecation warning headers | Per-request | Operator (audit logs) |
| Conformance test pass rate | Binary 100% or fail | Operator (Sonobuoy) |
| API endpoint coverage | Continuous % (~94% at v1.25) | Vendor (CNCF) |
| Pluto/Kubent/Kubepug scan results | Count of deprecated/removed APIs | Operator (CI/CD) |
| client-go compatibility | Matrix (✓/+/-) | Vendor (K8s project) |

## Gaps and Limitations

- `apiserver_requested_deprecated_apis` tracks requests, not stored resources — objects in etcd using old APIs are not captured unless re-requested
- Conformance test coverage (94% of endpoints) measures breadth, not depth — one test per endpoint may miss behavioral regressions
- No quantitative data on false positive/negative rates for Pluto, Kubent, or Kubepug
- "Deprecated APIs are the #1 upgrade failure cause" is widely cited but lacks a single authoritative quantitative study
- Static tools require separate runs and don't integrate into a unified pre-upgrade metric
